def: The part of prediction error caused by a model family too rigid to express the true relationship, even with unlimited data.
The part of prediction error caused by the fitted model changing from one training sample to the next.
The noise in the target itself, which no model can predict.
How many different shapes a model family can express, such as the degree of a polynomial.
A plot of training and validation error against training-set size, used to tell high bias from high variance.
Any change that makes a model less able to fit noise, at the cost of fitting the signal slightly worse.
Least squares with a penalty on the sum of squared weights (L2), which shrinks all weights and stabilises correlated features.
Least squares with a penalty on the sum of absolute weights (L1), which drives many weights exactly to zero.
A linear model penalised by a mix of the L1 and L2 norms of its weights.
A setting chosen by the practitioner, such as a penalty strength, rather than learned from the training loss.
An optimiser that updates one weight at a time while holding the others fixed, used to fit the lasso.
The operator that shrinks a value towards zero by a fixed amount and stops at zero, used in each lasso update.
Halting training when validation error stops improving, which keeps weights small and acts as a regulariser.
